description: Aborts an unpublished merge by operation_id, releasing its target fence, reservation and retained result. Recovers a published S3 result instead; uncertain remote outcomes retain state. Serialized with merge attempts.
Lists the branches of a differential database with their head snapshot and, for shared databases, their state relative to the S3 branch head.
example: SELECT branch_name, head_snapshot_id, remote_state FROM differential_branches('sales');

description: Takes a single-writer database's S3 branch heads over after a copy of the repository wrote them.
Deletes completed operation records and history entries of expired snapshots older than older_than; request IDs of deleted operations no longer replay.
example: SELECT table_name, rows FROM differential_cleanup_metadata(older_than => now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY, dry_run => true);

description: Collects local data that no snapshot, branch, pin or pending export references any more.

Garbage-collects an S3 location in two phases: condemns data no branch head or unexpired snapshot references, and deletes what stayed condemned and unreachable since before older_than (default: a week ago).
example: SELECT condemned_objects, deleted_bytes FROM differential_cleanup_remote_files('s3://my-bucket/lake/', dry_run => true);

description: Creates an independent database from a snapshot of another one, on the same data path and sharing its data.
Returns free pages of the repository's metadata store to the file system.
Creates a writable branch from a snapshot, sharing all data with it.
Checkpoints an attached writable branch and publishes it as an immutable snapshot with optional commit metadata; exports it to S3 and, for shared databases, moves the S3 branch head.
example: SELECT snapshot_id, export_state FROM differential_create_snapshot('sales', name => 'v1', message => 'first load');

description: Returns the snapshot an attachment reads, or the latest snapshot of the attached branch or database.
Lists the databases of the differential repository with their data path and writer mode.
example: SELECT database_name, data_path, writers FROM differential_databases();

description: Removes files in local pools that no mapping references, left behind by crashes.
Preserves a detached branch's contents as a snapshot and drops the branch (in a shared database, for every writer).
Drops the local copy of snapshots whose S3 export completed; they are then read through S3.
example: SELECT snapshot_id FROM differential_evict_snapshots('sales', versions => [1], dry_run => true);

description: Retires snapshots selected by version list and/or age so their local data can be collected; S3 exports remain.
example: SELECT snapshot_id FROM differential_expire_snapshots('sales', versions => [1], dry_run => true);

description: Lists this process's followers (ATTACH ... FOLLOW true): what each follows, the state it reads, when it last checked S3 and its last error.
example: SELECT alias, follows, epoch, checked_at FROM differential_followers();

description: Copies an offline native DuckDB file into a new differential database and publishes it as snapshot 1.
Inspects recorded local snapshot parents and best common ancestor candidates, including expired history. Incomplete and ambiguous history is reported without guessing a base.

Merges published local or single-writer S3 branch heads using a unique proven best common ancestor. Destination equal to ours updates that detached, clean target; otherwise creates a new branch. Returns merge_action (created_branch, merged, fast_forward, already_up_to_date). Optional expected_base_snapshot_id/expected_ours_snapshot_id/expected_theirs_snapshot_id must be supplied together and guard the reviewed selection. The request records its input snapshot selection and schema_mode once; source live changes are excluded. schema_mode => 'additive' allows supported new tables and nullable column additions; 'catalog' also merges table/nullable-column removals and view definitions.

Checks local or single-writer S3 branch merge readiness without publishing or recording a request. Returns selected input IDs, expected action, destination/target state, conflict counts and bounded diagnostics including pending recovery operations. Native final-state validation defaults to true. Checks are advisory; use expected snapshot IDs when executing.

Previews published branch heads using a unique proven best common ancestor. Returns resolved input IDs, counts and bounded typed conflicts; validate => true checks final constraints. schema_mode => 'additive' allows supported new tables and nullable column additions; 'catalog' also merges table/nullable-column removals and view definitions. Catalog conflicts are reported separately.

Inspects a bounded page of durable merge requests without S3 access. Includes inputs, destination, retained result, frozen schema policy, original branch identities, input guards, target fences and recovery guidance. Latest-attempt diagnostics include a count, phase, safe error code and timestamps; incomplete does not imply liveness. Ordered by operation_id; after_operation_id is an exclusive pagination cursor.
Reads the frozen typed resolution choices of a merge request. Does not read mutable resolution source tables.

Merges three explicit snapshots into a new branch after native constraint validation and checkpointing. Supports local and single-writer S3 storage; S3 publication is synchronous and recoverable. Conflicts prevent publication. schema_mode => 'catalog' also merges table/nullable-column removals and view definitions; 'additive' only allows supported table/column additions. The default is strict.

Compares three explicit snapshots of a local or single-writer S3 database using typed, cell-level merge rules. Returns per-table counts and byte-bounded typed conflict details; validate => true checks final constraints in disposable staging. schema_mode => 'additive' allows supported new tables and nullable column additions; 'catalog' also merges table/nullable-column removals and view definitions. Catalog conflicts are reported separately.
Lists active merges and previews in this process and repository, with phase, progress and resource counters. Durable request outcomes are in differential_merge_requests().
example: SELECT phase, tables_completed, tables_total FROM differential_merge_status();

description: Lists the durable operation records of the repository, used to replay requests by request_id.
example: SELECT kind, state, snapshot_id FROM differential_operations();

description: Lists the repository's storage locations (metadata store, local pools, S3 locations) with their S3 configuration and credential source, never credentials.

Recovers the newest shipped state of a branch (SHIP_WAL) from S3 into a new local database: its chain's base, read on demand, plus every shipped epoch; DuckDB replays the WAL at the first ATTACH. same_identity => true keeps the original identities (a failover of the writer).
Copies an exported snapshot from S3 into a new writable differential database, verifying every chunk.
Lists the branch heads exported to an S3 location, each with the path to ATTACH its latest snapshot.
Reconciles a diverged branch of a shared database with its S3 head, keeping local work as a new branch or as a local snapshot.
example: SELECT kept_snapshot_id, kept_branch FROM differential_resolve_conflict('team', keep => 'branch');

description: Resets a detached branch to a snapshot after preserving its current contents as a snapshot.
example: SELECT snapshot_id, preservation_snapshot_id FROM differential_restore('sales', 1, branch => 'dev');

description: Lists why each stored database image is retained (snapshots, branches, pins, exports).
Finishes pending S3 exports of a database (all, or one snapshot) and republishes its branch heads.
Lists every snapshot of a differential database (for a shared database also other writers' snapshots, read from S3) with commit metadata, publication and S3 export state.
example: SELECT snapshot_id, snapshot_name, export_state FROM differential_snapshots('sales');

description: Reports the extension's capabilities, durability profiles, limits and last background publication error as capability/status rows.
Returns storage, S3, cache and timing counters of the repository and process as metric/value rows.
example: SELECT metric, value FROM differential_storage_stats() WHERE metric = 'local_payload_bytes';

description: Lists the advisory 'being written' markers of a shared database in S3: which hosts are writing which branches.
example: SELECT branch_name, host, live FROM differential_writers('team');
